transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Well, I’m here mostly because everybody keeps saying I’m doing too much. My family, folks at church, even some of the younger guys at work—they act like I’m running myself ragged, but I don’t see it that way. I mean, somebody’s got to handle the move properly, and the new garage isn’t going to rebuild itself right, not if you want it square and lasting.

And then there’s church stuff—people mean well, but if you don’t organize it, it turns into a mess. Same thing at work. These younger fellows, they don’t always know how the job ought to be done unless someone shows them. So, I guess I’m here because they think it’s too much, but to me it feels like I’m just the one with enough drive to get it all done.
Have you felt unusually energetic, or like you can take on a lot more tasks than usual, even if others think you might be overdoing it?

Yes, I suppose I have. I don’t think of it as “unusual,” exactly, but everybody keeps saying I’m taking on too much. To me it feels like I’m the only one with enough drive to get the move handled right, and then the garage at the new place needs rebuilding proper—not some slapdash job, you know, because my father always said if a thing’s worth doing, you make it square.

And church, well, they mean well, but somebody has to organize things or it all gets sideways. Then at work, the younger fellows still need showing how the job ought to be done. So yes, I guess I’ve been doing a lot, but it feels necessary more than anything.
Have you noticed any time recently where your mood was significantly elevated, where you felt unusually happy, irritable, or 'on top of the world' for a period of time?

Well… yes, I guess you could call it that. I’ve had times lately where I feel like, you know, everybody just needs to get on board with what I’m trying to do or get out of the way. Not in a mean way, necessarily, but there’s a right way to handle things.

And I’ll be joking around, feeling big as life—like I’m ten feet tall—and then my wife or my boy asks me some little question, and I snap. Then they look at me like I’ve done something awful. But sometimes it feels like they’re slowing me down when I’m trying to keep everything moving.
Can you describe how long these periods of feeling 'big as life' or unusually confident have lasted? Have there been times when this was noticeably different from how you usually feel?

I’d say it’s been… oh, about a month now, give or take. Since we had to start leaving the old house. That whole thing set everything in motion, you know—packing, sorting, people touching things they don’t understand, deciding what goes where like they know better.

But yes, since then I’ve felt different than my usual self, I suppose. More… geared up. More certain I can get it all handled, if everybody would just let me do it right.
Have you found yourself needing less sleep lately, like you can get by on just a few hours and still feel full of energy?

I’m not sure I’ve been keeping track of it that way. I mean, sleep’s always a funny thing, isn’t it? Some nights you lie there thinking about one thing or another, and then the clock looks different than you thought it would. My wife could probably tell you better than I can—she notices all that.

But getting by on just a few hours and feeling full of energy… I don’t know. I wouldn’t want to say that exactly. I’ve just had a lot on my mind, and once I’m up, I’m up, you know? Hard to tell what’s “less sleep” and what’s just being busy.
Have you found yourself doing things that were unusual for you—like spending more money than usual, making big plans quickly, or acting impulsively in any way?

Well… I wouldn’t call it impulsive exactly. I mean, when a garage needs work, it needs work, and if you wait around for everybody to agree on every little thing, nothing ever gets done.

But I did put some deposits down—garage work, some equipment—without really talking it through with my wife first. She wasn’t happy about that. And I’ve been going back and forth between the houses a lot, trying to keep things moving, and at the plant I’ve maybe rushed a few jobs more than I should’ve. People said I was taking chances, but sometimes people say that when they don’t understand the job. Still… I guess it was more than usual for me.
Has there been a time in the past month where you felt this way—'big as life,' very confident, or irritable—for most of the day, nearly every day, and it lasted for at least a week straight?

Yeah… I suppose there has been. I don’t know if I’d mark it on a calendar exactly, but it’s been most days, pretty much all day, where I feel like people need to either get on board with what I’m trying to do or just get out of my way.

And it flips, you know? One minute I’m joking around, feeling ten feet tall, like I can handle the whole mess myself—and then my wife or my boy asks one little question and I snap at them. Then they look at me like I’m the problem, but I’m just trying to keep things moving.

Can you recall if there was a time in the past month when you felt unusually upbeat, irritable, or energized for at least four days straight—like you were on a roll and could get everything done without getting tired?

Yeah, I mean… four days, sure, it’s been longer than that, I think. It’s not like I wake up and say, “Well, day three of feeling this way,” you know?

But I’ve been on edge and charged up, like everyone needs to either get on board with what I’m trying to do or just get out of my way. And sometimes I’m joking, feeling ten feet tall, like I can handle the whole thing myself… then my wife or my boy asks some little question and I snap at them. It’s stupid, because they’re not doing anything terrible, but in the moment it feels like they’re slowing me down.
Can you tell me if there was a time when you felt this way—like you were on top of the world or unusually irritable—for seven full days in a row without a break?

Seven full days… yeah, I think so. It’s sort of been running together, honestly. I’ve been feeling like everybody needs to either get on board with what I’m trying to do or just get out of my way.

And it’s not all one thing, either—I’ll be joking around, feeling ten feet tall, like I can handle everything myself, and then my wife or my boy asks me some little question and I snap. Like they’re holding me up, even if they’re just asking. So yeah… I’d say it’s been going on like that without much of a break.

Can you recall a specific time in the past month when your mood was clearly different from usual—like being unusually high, excited, or irritable—for a full seven days straight, where it felt like your mood was driving everything you did?

Yeah… I can recall it, though it’s all kind of blurred together. It was like my mood was running the whole show. I’ve been feeling like everybody needs to either get on board with what I’m planning or just get out of my way.

And, you know, I’ll be laughing and carrying on, feeling ten feet tall, like I can do everything myself—like back when I was working and you just had to keep the machine going, no time for people standing around asking the same thing twice—and then my wife or my boy asks me some small question and I snap at them. Not even a big thing. Just a question. But right then it feels like they’re slowing me down. So yeah, it was different from my usual, and it lasted like that.
